script: What if your memory reset every single day? Not just names. Everything. You wake up with a note on your hand, in your own handwriting. You read the wall. It's covered in sticky notes you wrote yourself. Day one, you watch your favorite movie, and every twist still shocks you. Every night, your little brother Sam gives you a piano lesson, and every morning you forget it. Day thirty, his school pianist gets sick, so you walk on stage and play the whole concert without one wrong note. But every morning, a girl in purple waits by your bed with a photo of you two. She smiles and says, I'm Mia, your best friend. You've never seen her before. Because the seahorse-shaped part of your brain that saves each day while you sleep has stopped saving. But skills are stored somewhere else. That's why real people with memory loss like yours have learned to draw in a mirror without remembering a single lesson. Your hands remember. Your heart doesn't. Day one hundred, you find Mia crying in the hallway. Every morning, you look at me like a stranger. That night, the pen is in your hand, and sleep is coming. Ten seconds. Nine. Eight. Write, she's your best friend. Seven. Six. Or write, let her go. Five. Four. She stays and gets hurt every single morning, or she leaves, and you'll never know she existed. What do you write on your hand?
title: What If Your Memory Reset Every Day?
